project.name: plumb-core
project.description:
LAYER 1 -- the foundation. These modules know nothing about dataflow analysis and nothing about each other beyond what is listed here:
- plumb-parser the Java source parser and the Java language-level resolution (Java 8..25). - plumb-rules the rule identifiers, parameters and registry -- the vocabulary every checker speaks. - plumb-reporter the finding model and the report writers.
WHY THE LAYERS ARE AGGREGATORS AND NOT DIRECTORIES. The modules keep their top-level directories, and this POM groups them for the BUILD. Two reasons, both learned the hard way:
1. The repository's gate scripts resolve module paths from the repository root. scripts/check_test_coverage.py DISCOVERS modules by iterating the root directory (REPO.iterdir()) and complains about any module with tests that it does not know about. Move a module into a subdirectory and that gate stops SEEING it -- it does not fail, it silently stops checking, which is worse than no gate. 43 gate scripts resolve module paths as REPO / "plumb-NAME".
2. Moving a module is a path change, not a design change, and it buys nothing that the reactor order does not already give: Maven orders the reactor by the dependency graph, so the layer boundaries are already enforced at build time whether or not they are declared here.
So the layering is expressed in the BUILD (this POM and the two beside it), and the source tree stays flat and greppable. A reader asks "what depends on what?" and gets one answer from the POMs, not a second one from directory nesting.
